# User-defined opcodes

A user-defined opcode (UDO) is a reusable Csound operation. Open **Window →
Editors → UDOs** to manage definitions saved in the current project. Blue
generates these definitions in `<CsInstruments>` before the project's
[Orchestra](orchestra.qmd) instruments.

## Create and edit a project UDO

1. Click **Add** in the UDO list, then select the new row.
2. Enter an **Opcode Name** and choose **Classic** or **Modern** under
   **Style**. For Classic, supply **Out Types** and **In Types**. For Modern,
   supply **Out Types** and named **Input Arguments**.
3. Enter the operation body on the **Code** tab. Blue generates the opcode
   declaration and ending from the fields, so the body should omit `opcode`
   and `endop` lines. The **Comments** tab stores notes about the definition.
4. Click **Test Opcode** to preview the Csound code Blue generates for this
   definition. To check it with Csound, use it in an instrument and render
   the project. **Project → Generate CSD to Screen** shows its placement in
   the full project.

The project UDO list has **Add** and **Import** controls. Import accepts a
Blue UDO (`.blueUDO`) or a Csound UDO (`.udo`, `.orc`, or `.csd`). A row's
context menu offers **Export**, **Remove**, and **Push Up** or **Push Down**.
Blue emits project UDOs in list order, which matters when one definition
uses another.

## Reuse definitions

The separate **Libraries** panel has **User Libraries → User-Defined Opcodes**
for definitions you want to reuse in other projects. Copy or drag a library
UDO into the project's UDO list; the project receives its own definition.
Insertion keeps the opcode name, even if the list already contains that name.
Review the list and rename definitions and their calls when necessary.
An instrument can also carry embedded UDOs. Use an embedded definition when
the instrument should bring its opcode with it when copied to another
project. During CSD generation, Blue reuses equivalent embedded definitions.
If an embedded definition has the same name as a different project definition,
Blue gives it a generated name such as `uniqueUDO0` and updates calls in the
instrument and its dependent embedded UDOs. This changes the generated CSD;
the project's stored definitions retain their names and code. See
[Orchestra](orchestra.qmd) for instrument editing.

The older Java manual shows a different UDO manager and links to external
collections. Consult the upstream Blue 2 edition for those historical instructions;
use the current controls described here for Blue 3.
